distinct prostate cancer-related mRNA cargos are found within MVs and EXO subpopulations from prostate cell lines.
the prostate cell lines PC-3 and PNT2, as well as LNCaP and PNT2 cell lines, release extracellular vesicles that contain distinct prostate cancer-related mRNA cargos.
the mRNA cargo in prostate cancer-derived EVs differs based on the EV type, the cellular origin of the vesicles, and the subpopulation of EVs studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of prostate cancer-related mRNA in EV subpopulations and their potential use as diagnostic biomarkers.
the development and validation of new biomarker candidates for prostate cancer diagnosis.

the characterization of prostate cancer-related mRNA cargoes in EV subsets from prostate cell cultures, which could provide a novel source of biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mRNA cargo in prostate cancer-derived EVs depends on the type and subpopulation of the analyzed EVs and the cell origin.
the prostate cancer-related mRNA content of MVs and/or EXOs is highly dependent on the cell line of origin and on the EV subpopulation analyzed.
the mRNA cargo in EVs from prostate cell lines is distinct and depends on the cell line analyzed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mRNA cargo in MVs and EXOS from different cell lines is distinct and that the mRNA cargo is more abundant in MVs than in EXOs.

MVs and EXO subsets derived from prostate cells carry a distinct prostate cancer-related mRNA signature, and the mRNA profile of EVs can differ depending on the EV subpopulation analyzed and cellular origin.
the mRNA cargo in prostate cell-derived MVs is more abundant and diverse than in EXOs and that prostate cell-derived MV mRNA cargo is more variable than that of prostate cell-derived EXOs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EV subpopulation should be considered when studying EVs and that the mRNA cargo can differ based on the cellular origin of the EVs.
the mRNA cargo in prostate cancer cell-derived MVs and EXOS is highly distinct from that of benign prostate cells.
the mRNA cargo is different in the EV subpopulations, and the EV subpopulation should be carefully selected when analyzing mRNA in EVs.
